items.title: Color hardening (C3): does the jade survive a cheap monitor
items.note: HARDENED PER D23; owner on-device confirmation pending as the closing check. Owner read the bench on two machines (high-end display as control, standard laptop as the OPERATIVE floor) and returned floors A06 / B06 / E1-07 / E2-05, glass 0.75 and 0.60, D-L04 exempt (WCAG 1.4.3), F1+F3 collapsing. Twelve token values moved, each converted through the bench's own mix(from,to,k) at the read rung rather than re-invented: bg fafbfc->f5f7f9, surface-hover f3f5f8->e7ebf1, surface-tint f4f9f7->e9f3ef, surface-alt f5f7fa->ebeff5, input-bg f7f9fb->eff3f7, border ebedf1->c3c9d5, border-strong dcdfe4->969fae, surface-tint-border dbeae3->93c0ab, ink-surface 12201b->192b24, on-ink-border 35504a->405e58, on-ink-border-strong 4a6b60->5b8275, ink-hover 264035->2e4d40. THREE JUDGMENT CALLS, all recorded in docs/COLOR_BENCH.md section 6. (1) ink-hover is the one token no reading set, and forcing B06's 2.0x onto it produced a REAL AA FAILURE - on-ink-muted fell 5.85:1 to 3.15:1 - because it is a nav-row hover FILL WITH TEXT ON IT, not the raised card the B ladder measured. Re-derived from its own two constraints instead: text 4.85:1 with margin AND separation RISES to 1.59:1 from 1.50:1. Where a floor and AA conflict, AA wins. (2) Glass HELD and F1 adopted only in half: the C1 floor 0.75 sits BELOW the shipped 0.90, so the alpha already cleared its floor and floors-only-rise gives no mandate to move it; the fragment's collapse was the EDGE, so the edge moved (divider tier -> card tier on a token itself hardened, so 2.85:1 -> 3.47:1 vs the surface it actually sits on - the 'strong' tier finally meets the 3:1 floor it is NAMED for and had never met there). (3) F3's rule half shipped to all 15 section and sticky-chrome boundaries while the 34 CARD edges stayed on --border; the band half was deliberately NOT a blanket swap, because the site already alternates --bg against --surface-tint and tinting every --bg section would leave EVERY section tinted and destroy the white register the tonal map is built on. WATCH: --accent on --surface-tint is 4.54:1, the tightest margin in the palette, 0.04 above AA - darkening the tint fails accent text on it.

items.title: FO-2: scrolled-nav edge made scale-proof + I21 painted-edge invariant
items.note: A field report that the instruments DISAGREED with, and the disagreement was the finding. The reported suspects were all about the edge not being painted; measurement showed it was painted everywhere, at the exact token colour, on 3 engines x 4 DSFs, armed every time. The real cause was perceptual polarity - a monotonic mid-step inside a 13:1 dark-to-light transition is read as antialiasing however correct its contrast ratio is - and it explains BOTH of the owner's observations with one mechanism: the /platform rule they called crisp is a local extremum, the nav edge was not. It also explains why the D23 bench missed it: the F1 fragment was titled 'Nav over ink', and over ink the edge always worked. TWO INSTRUMENT FAULTS were found and recorded, because each nearly produced a false finding: a smooth-scroll artifact (scroll-behavior:smooth means scrollTo animates, and frames captured mid-flight show the sticky bar unrepositioned - the seam appeared MISSING at three of four scroll positions until every scroll was made behavior:'instant'), and an extremum detector that was wrong twice (comparing the global minimum against the plateaus fails because at this seam the global minimum IS the bar; comparing against immediate neighbours fails because at DSF 2 a 1px border is two identical rows and neither is a STRICT extremum). Both lessons are written into the invariant file.

items.title: FO-3 investigation: zoom-class reproduction attempt + I20 zoom leg (no fix - held)

items.title: FO-3 fix: van moved inside the svg, LUT transform positioning, offset-path system removed
items.note: POSITIONING IS A PRECOMPUTED LUT: at each geometry change the rendered path is sampled at N=256 points into two Float32Arrays; per frame update() interpolates two entries and writes ONE transform attribute. Zero per-frame geometry reads, zero per-frame layout reads - the scroll handler is still one passive listener, one rAF, one CSS var write. MEASURED: LUT build 15.3ms chromium / 12ms webkit / 30ms firefox, paid once per geometry change and never per frame; per-frame 4.9us / 3.7us / 13.8us against a 16667us frame, i.e. 0.02 to 0.08 percent of budget. N WAS CHOSEN BY MEASUREMENT: the straight leg interpolates exactly so error exists only in the terminus curve, where chord error is about s^2/(8R) = 19^2/(8*460) = 0.10px, 10x under I20's 1px tolerance and measured at 0.095-0.106px. N=512 halved the error to 0.03px (imperceptible) while costing 144ms on firefox per rebuild - a visible main-thread stall on a reflow mid-scroll, bought with accuracy nobody can see. MOTION PARITY VERIFIED IN ALL THREE ENGINES, not hoped: three nested groups each own exactly one transform so none of them fight (.route-van the per-frame translate as a presentation ATTRIBUTE so no CSS rule may set transform on it, .route-van-lane the +/-12px lane at 450ms, .route-van-nose the +/-90deg facing at 200ms); rotation displaces the van centre by 0.00px, the leg flip moves it by exactly -24.00px, nose matrices exactly +/-90deg. Eye pass at zoom 1: worst delta 0.09px over 30 slow steps and 0.01px on hard jumps with no settle - BETTER than the Task #19 baseline of 0.227/0.08. Handoff holds at 36px through the curve, the U-turn, the manual reflow trigger and its removal; I15 gap 21px unchanged. SUPPORT GAINED: the @supports (offset-path) gate used to HIDE THE VAN ENTIRELY on engines without offset-path; SVG transforms need no gate, so the van now renders wherever the svg does. A MEASUREMENT SUBTLETY that looked like a 12px regression and was not: getBoundingClientRect on a <g> INCLUDES its children's transforms, so it folds in the deliberate lane offset - the old HTML parent's border box excluded it for free. I20 now measures van.getScreenCTM(), the group's own origin, which is the point that rides the path. || TASK #25 SUPERSEDES THE EVIDENCE, NOT THE ARCHITECTURE. The conviction narrative this entry recorded rested on a probe that read the progress variable from the wrong element and therefore printed 0 on every machine; it is retracted. The single-surface architecture stands on its independently measured merits: one raster surface, gate removal, 4.9 to 13.8us per frame, invariant coverage. The actual root cause of FO-3 was an invalid CSS length in stroke-dashoffset, found and fixed in Task #25.

items.title: FO-3 root cause: invalid CSS length in stroke-dashoffset (Gecko drew the whole path)
items.note: A one-line CSS defect that had been shipping since the route was built, hidden by two engines being permissive. stroke-dashoffset calc(1 - var(...)) is invalid because the property takes a length and a bare number is not one. Blink and WebKit coerce it; Gecko correctly drops the declaration, so the offset falls back to 0 and dasharray 1 paints the whole path. The line rendered fully drawn while the van, positioned by a JS transform that never consults CSS inheritance, sat correctly at mid-route. THE INSTRUMENT THAT FOUND IT WAS THE ONE THAT MEASURED WHAT THE LINE ACTUALLY CLAIMS rather than what the code intends: reading the computed stroke-dashoffset directly. Both previous field probes had assumed their way past this. Fixed by multiplying by 1px; verified in all three engines; I20 now asserts the line agrees with the variable, and a dpr-2 lane was added to the zoom leg. The dpr-2 lead that opened this hunt was a red herring, measured identical in Gecko at dpr 1, 1.5 and 2. FIELD-CLOSED 2026-08-20: varP 0.6523 = lineP 0.6523 on the owner laptop at dpr 2 - the px-units fix confirmed on real hardware, with build provenance established.

items.title: W5 part 2a: motion-safe architecture conversion + motion guard + nexo-motion skill v1
items.note: THE ARCHITECTURE IS INVERTED. Motion used to be declared in the base rules and patched off by a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block of !important overrides, which made the accessible rendering a SUBTRACTION from the animated one - the static state was whatever survived the overrides, and a new transition added without a matching override would have shipped silently. Now the base IS the static final composition and motion is strictly additive, declared only inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference), Tailwind's motion-safe: variant, or a [data-*-live] armed-attribute selector whose arming code early-returns on the reduced-motion query. CONVERSION COUNTS: 37 CSS declarations lifted across 28 selectors (25 unlayered, 3 re-emitted inside @layer utilities so layered styles are not silently promoted above unlayered ones), 15 rules emptied by the lift and removed whole, the 669-byte reduce-override block deleted, and 29 Tailwind utilities prefixed across 11 files - 66 conversions in total. ALREADY COMPLIANT AND DELIBERATELY NOT REFACTORED (impact check): 29 declarations under [data-*-live] armed attributes, verified in source at RouteOverlay.tsx, TerminusReveal.tsx, AssistScene.tsx, MapObserver.tsx and ProofBand.tsx. DEAD CODE FOUND AND DELETED: src/components/motion/Reveal.tsx and PageTransition.tsx, the ONLY two consumers of framer-motion, imported by nothing - PageTransition's own comment claimed it was used by (public)/template.tsx, which does not exist. Also dead: the reduce block's button:active transform override, which suppressed nothing because no active: transform utility exists anywhere in src. THE GUARD: scripts/qa/static-motion-check.mjs, zero-dep, character-level CSS parse plus string-literal-scoped TSX scan, wired into qa:static so BOTH seams (the qa:sweep prelude and the CI check job) pick it up with one edit, exactly as the type and hex guards did. Negative-tested on six legs: three plants caught with file and line (bare utility, bare CSS transition, animation scoped only to Radix data-state) and two sanctioned scopes correctly accepted, plus a clean control. THE KEY DISTINCTION THE GUARD ENCODES: Radix data-state and the components own data-active / data-level / data-leg are set REGARDLESS of the motion preference and therefore do NOT sanction a motion declaration; only [data-*-live] does. This task's own first inventory pass got that wrong and counted 40 declarations as compliant when the real number was 29.

items.title: D27 receipts + Railway nav dissection + Grand Bench roster
items.note: Docs and research only: no site code, no cube, because nothing the cube covers moved. Ground truth to v2.0 with D27 appended. Twelve suggestion entries S-015 to S-026, one per directive plus the liquid-nav note, the platform per-section animation wish (LATER), the console-fill verdict CLOSED (owner reviewed, edge-carries-separation doctrine stands), and the scheduled framer-motion removal. W1, W2, W5 and W6 rescoped citing D27. RAILWAY DISSECTED LIVE at CSS level into DESIGN_RESEARCH section 15, five-field method, verdict table of 11 elements. THE HEADLINE FINDING CUTS AGAINST THE BRIEF: Railway's nav bar background is rgb(19,17,28) and the page body is rgb(19,17,28) - the same value - with no backdrop-filter, no border-bottom, no shadow, and it is UNCHANGED when scrolled. Railway has no boundary and never acquires one, so it cannot be the answer to D27a's 'boundary perceivable at a glance'. What it does supply is the panel: a pure-black panel darker than the page, with destination cells filled at the PAGE colour, 6px radius and NO borders - separation is fill-against-fill rather than a drawn edge, which is one extra colour value and zero borders. Hover is a +5/+5/+6 fill lift and nothing else. The panel animates its HEIGHT between triggers, measured 266 to 296 at 80ms to 302 at 120ms, which is nexo-shape with a live reference implementation. Their down-page background IS the product's own canvas - dotted field, service nodes with live status, connectors - which is the strongest reference found for D27e. Perf observed at 4814ms DCL, 299 requests, at least 3854KB: 4x, 5x and 6.4x our D20 ceilings, and NONE of it buys the nav, so D20 is not in tension with D27. Grand Bench roster written as docs/GRAND_BENCH_PLAN.md with per-candidate purpose, fragments, interaction, binding laws and what the owner will judge.

items.title: The Grand Bench rendered (B1-B5 + composite)
items.note: One self-contained file://-ready page, docs/grand-bench/index.html, 18 fragments, real D21/D23/D25 tokens, real approved copy, sticky legend, BY CANDIDATE / BY REGISTER group-by, and a B1-to-COMPOSITE index. NO SITE CODE AND NO CUBE: it is tooling. The bench DOGFOODS the motion-safe architecture it models - every animation lives inside a no-preference media query, the B1 panel morph uses a retargetable TRANSITION rather than a keyframe (the fault found in the shipped nav in #29), and the reduced-motion pass reports ZERO running animations with every fragment complete and static. Braid geometry is authored at build time as literal path data so nothing depends on page JS. VERIFIED: 102 painted-pixel spot ratios over the new surfaces, ZERO below floor; fonts primed and all three families confirmed loaded; zero console errors; no horizontal overflow at 1440, 768 or 390; heading sequence clean with zero jumps; 14/14 tabbed elements show a focus indicator. THE PAINTED-PIXEL PASS EARNED ITS KEEP by catching two defects a computed ratio cannot see: the Solutions menu was rendering ON TOP of the Platform menu because .panel-grid{display:grid} beats the UA [hidden] rule, and drift dots were sitting under body copy at 3.9:1. Both fixed. impeccable audit run: 3 detector findings, one false positive proven by measurement, one real and reduced, one real and intentional with its cost now stated on the bench.

items.title: D28 receipts + the Noir Bench (N1-N5 + composite)
items.note: Docs and research only: no site code, no cube. THE CRAFTED VALUES: electric mint #2fe89a (hue 155, S80 V91, 11.62:1 on ink), alternate #00ffa3 (hue 158, S100 V100, 14.01:1), and the light-register mint #00a36a (3.03:1 on paper). THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: electric mint DIES on paper at 1.49:1, so the neon is register-split - electric is an INK-register idea, and on light the same line reads as precision rather than as voltage. Charcoal tunings composite to #bdc1c4 (1.69:1) and #9ba0a4 (2.46:1) against D23's E1-07 divider floor of 1.66, and invert on ink to #333d3e (1.66:1). VERIFIED: 57 painted-pixel runs over the new surfaces with ZERO below floor; reduced-motion pass with zero running animations and zero strands unpainted; zero console errors; zero horizontal overflow at 1440, 768 and 390; heading sequence clean; 12/12 focus indicators; fonts primed. A LAW COLLISION IS NAMED RATHER THAN RESOLVED: nexo-brand section 5 bans glow on objects and D28 asks for glowing neon borders, so both N4 treatments use a tight ring rather than a halo and the amendment is put to the owner.

decisions.title: Impact-check law + design suggestion register
decisions.summary: (a) Every future build prompt carries an IMPACT CHECK step before implementation: map the planned change against the section-4 ledger, the FIXLOG AUDIT GUIDANCE lines, and the invariant set; name every collision and how it is resolved. An unresolvable collision is a STOP-and-surface-to-owner fork, never a silent override. (b) All design and feature suggestions from any source - owner, Claude, external AI reviews, user feedback - are captured in docs/DESIGN_SUGGESTIONS.md with source, date, disposition (ADOPTED / ALREADY-LAW / TEST-FIRST / LATER / REJECTED-with-reason / OWNER-DIRECTIVE) and impact notes citing D-numbers and invariants. Nothing is implemented from suggestion lists directly: register first, impact-check at adoption time. WHY THIS LAW EXISTS NOW: the external design audit that prompted it reviewed the LIVE V1 site, and one of its prescriptions - remove all drop shadows - collides head-on with the F1 nav seam shipped in Task #20, which IS a box-shadow hairline fixing a field failure and is guarded by I21. A plausible-sounding suggestion applied without an impact check would have re-opened a closed field defect and failed an invariant.

decisions.title: Build-environment integrity law (file sync, field provenance, probe publication)
decisions.summary: D25 is HELD for the pending colour-direction ruling per the bench protocol; this row is numbered D26 so the reserved slot stays open. (a) File sync must never touch build exhaust: a committed .stignore at the repo root excludes .next, node_modules, .git and out. Syncthing reads .stignore from the folder root, so committing it protects every machine automatically after a git pull. The owner syncs the working folder across three machines, which is a live mechanism for stale and mixed builds and the most likely contaminant of two earlier field rounds. (b) FIELD PROVENANCE PROTOCOL: every field test begins with the build-generation probe, and screenshots of unproven builds are not evidence. PROBE PUBLICATION RULE: any field probe published into docs/FIELD_OBSERVATIONS.md must FIRST be executed by the harness against the running local build, with its output shown in the task report, and must be derived from the actual rendered DOM and CSS rather than assumed selectors. Untested probes are banned. Two chat-authored probes were published blind and both failed: one read the progress variable from documentElement when the code sets it on .route-overlay, so it printed 0 on every machine forever; the other crashed on parseFloat of calc(0.72px), which is Blink serialisation of stroke-dashoffset. Both produced numbers that were cited as evidence and were artifacts. (c) Containerization (owner suggestion, S-013) registered for post-launch evaluation.

decisions.title: Colour direction ruled: D2 SYNTHESIS (owner)
decisions.summary: Jade remains the identity and owns all interactive, primary and status surfaces; warmth enters as ATMOSPHERE ONLY - layered CSS radial glows, background register, never carrying semantic meaning and never behind the alarms colour space. Owner-supplied anchor rose #f58f9c with companion #f7929a. Supporting owner picks registered for benched accent use only: violet #8d6fd3 (converges with the existing illustration accent family) and deep tones #332750 and #522a22 (ink-accent candidates, unadopted). OWNER STATED LAW ON RECORD: warm and pink cannot be an emergency-adjacent signal, incorporate it in backgrounds. That sentence is what makes the direction rulable, because it converts warmth from an identity question into a background-register question and leaves the alarms and the jade accent untouched. Implementation law: zero-cost CSS radials per the GitLab dissection, credited; every text-over-glow pairing AA-verified against PAINTED pixels rather than composited alphas; D23 floors bind and floors-only-rise is untouched; the final temperature is the owner pick from the tuned bench; site implementation is a separate full-cube task.

decisions.title: The Boldness Ruling (owner)
decisions.summary: Verdict on the current build: ~85% right - smooth, sleek, disciplined - but TOO QUIET: flat nav, decorative-but-mute background lines, list-shaped navigation, newspaper feel. Eight directives. (a) NAV becomes bold and unmistakable: sleek but heavy presence, liquid-glass weight, boundary perceivable at a glance, colour no longer restricted to black/ink. (b) NAV PANELS follow the boxed-destination pattern (Railway reference): each destination a designed box with its own shape and representation, never a text list. (c) HERO: the dispatch console demotes down-page and a big signature animation leads, activating D19/W2 with priority. (d) MOBILITY CARDS: the three service levels (ambulatory, wheelchair, stretcher, with bariatric and two-person assist as the modifier) rendered as beautiful switching cards in the GitLab dark-card register - this is S-001's concrete form. (e) AMBIENT MEANING: background lines must read as an intentional system model, aggressive, legible, semantic, never unexplained decoration. (f) BRAIDED ROUTE: evolve the single route line toward a braided multi-strand motif weaving the D25 rose and violet with the jade lead. (g) EVERY PAGE: per-page atmosphere attention in P4, no page ships as bare paper. (h) INTENTIONALITY DOCTRINE: every visual element must be able to state its purpose; 'just a nice line' is banned. PERCEPTION SUPERSESSION: the FO-2 nav hairline measures painted and I21 is green, but it reads invisible to the owner - recorded as the SUBTLE APPROACH FAILING THE OWNER'S BAR, not as a defect; I21 remains the floor; the bold nav supersedes the question. All directives flow through the Grand Bench (rendered candidates, owner reaction) before site application. D23 floors, the D20 budget, motion-safe architecture, decline-don't-degrade, and status-semantics law bind every candidate.

decisions.title: Tech-noir ruling (owner, Grand Bench reading)
decisions.summary: Brand thesis: a medical transportation company whose backbone is pure technology; trust through a clean, highly professional interface; the aesthetic of a modern high-end developer tool or cloud platform, Railway-class; minimalist and modern with a very subtle Blade Runner edge; practical medical transport made effortless through advanced routing tech. RULINGS: B1 adopt B1(i) INK-BOLD nav. B2 adopt structure, with active and hover carried by glowing neon accent borders rather than heavy fills, geometric utilitarian icons, and the modifier tier ratified. B3 adopt the braid at ROUTE SCALE for precision routing rather than page dominance; the strand palette is re-ruled so inactive strands are low-opacity neutral charcoal, register-aware, receding into the field, with ONE saturated neon active line, ELECTRIC MINT from the jade family - cyan remains rejected per S-007; van livery B, the ink body with mint outline glowing wireframe; the weave, the occlusion and the roller-coaster timing are unchanged because the recolor is paint-only. B4 adopt Direction 2, the dispatch-network model, as a tactical data stream. B5 drift REJECTED on bench evidence that the static field read better and that B4-d2 makes it redundant; settle ADOPTED as the arrival grammar. Composite ratifies Chanel's rule: the braid and the network nodes are THE signatures and everything around them stays stark and minimal. GUARDRAIL, load-bearing: subtle. Noir owns the signature and chrome registers only; D18 deep-reading surfaces for provider and payer content stay clean and legible; neon never carries or neighbours alarm semantics. OPEN FORK: the D25 warm atmosphere on ink is ruled from the Noir Bench fragment N3, not in chat.

decisions.title: Monochrome + One Light (owner research ruling)
decisions.summary: PALETTE LAW: deep ink, charcoal, stark white, and exactly ONE accent. Accent law verbatim: mint only where blood is pumping through the system - the accent marks life in the system (active route, live state, the one thing moving) and nowhere else, so an accent placed where nothing is live violates this law even when it is legible. The accent is ELECTRIC MINT #2fe89a, hue 155 degrees, 11.62:1 on ink; the maximum-voltage alternate #00ffa3 is rejected as gaming-adjacent because the brand is an instrument, not a console. REGISTER-SPLIT LAW, arithmetic rather than preference: electric mint measures 1.49:1 on paper and is unusable there for text or graphics, no tuning escapes it because it is a property of white grounds, so the light register carries its own active line (#00a36a, 3.03:1) and electric is an INK-register idea - on ink the signature reads as voltage, on light the same signature reads as precision. Jade as a wash is retired but jade SURVIVES as the mint bloodline, since electric mint sits inside the jade family at hue 155, so the identity is continuous rather than replaced, and cyan stays rejected per S-007 by measurement (cyan begins near 175 degrees, this sits 20 degrees clear). Rose and violet are retired including the illustration accent, with a noir pass over the line art scheduled. Section 5 amendment to nexo-brand: neon edges are 1px calibrated RINGS, never halos or blooms, per the N4-A expensive-instrument reading; the object-glow ban is otherwise intact and this amends section 5 for the signature and chrome registers only. Spring physics ship via CSS linear(), zero JS, so framer-motion stays dead. Ambient density is pursued through breathing and grain candidates, which are distinct from the rejected drift: drift was per-cell opacity cycling and read as moving parts, while density treatments change the field's texture rather than its behaviour, so S-028 is not reopened.

decisions.title: Two-Register Law + Seam Rule (owner, the Stripe move)
decisions.summary: The site runs two registers and each has a job it must do. THEATER, noir plus neon: chrome, heroes, the braid and van, the dispatch map, the mobility cards - its job is to prove technical weight. PAPER, light and high-legibility: provider requirements, payer content, compliance, and every D18 deep-reading surface - its job is to pass compliance. THE SEAM RULE: chrome is always theater on every page, so the bar does not change register when the body does; any page may open with a theater band; the moment content becomes studied (tables, floors, legal text, long-form) the page crosses to paper and STAYS there rather than crossing back inside one page; forms are paper; alarms are register-independent and keep their own colour space in both, which restates the D28 guardrail as a boundary rather than a warning. Each page's crossing point is drawn explicitly in that page's P4 tonal map, homepage first, so the seam is a designed line rather than an emergent one. Owner-approved scope: the homepage mid-page bands are re-cast into theater per the tonal map, which supersedes tonal map v3's register assignments for those bands; the map is redrawn in the task that implements it (#37) rather than inferred in advance.

decisions.title: D25 reversal receipt (ruled 08-20, shipped in #27, reversed 08-21 by N3-b)
decisions.summary: The warm-atmosphere direction is reversed after a side-by-side render rather than in prose. Owner, verbatim: the warm dusk is officially dead, mint is the only light in the dark. FROM: rose and violet atmosphere as an ink-register background wash (--atmo-rose #f58f9c, --atmo-rose-soft #f7929a, --atmo-violet #8d6fd3, --atmo-light, --atmo-ink) plus the compensated ink pair that existed only to pay for the wash's luminance lift (--ink-surface #273a32, --on-ink-border #4a6c66, --on-ink-border-strong #688f82). TO: pure noir per D29. WHY: side by side the warm atmosphere read as dusk rather than as instrumentation, and it put a second temperature into a palette whose whole argument is one light in the dark. SALVAGE, because the ruling cost nothing and produced three things that outlive it: the painted-pixel method (Range client rects in document coordinates against a text-hidden full-page raster), which is now the standard instrument; the register-split discovery, which is the seed of D29's register-split law; and the compensated-pair math, which is the worked example of what a background change costs in border and surface tokens. EXECUTION RIDES TASK #33, not #32 - the reversal removes the atmo applications and tokens, and the pre-#27 global values are intact outside the scoped .atmo-ink subtree, which #33 verifies before deleting rather than assuming.

decisions.title: R2 rulings + the Mint Restraint Law (owner)
decisions.summary: G1-b ADOPTED: the liquid-glass nav, tint at the 0.75 D23 lineage floor, blur 16px, over both registers, with the @supports fallback rendering solid ink-bold - the two-state reality is accepted by ruling rather than treated as a defect, and the nav must be complete and I21-legal in both. The braid's mint smearing through the glass is LEGAL: it is transmission of a live element rather than accent application, which is the interpretive note on D29's accent law - the mint is not placed in the chrome, it is seen through it. G2 breathing field ADOPTED for theater fields, with the imperceptible-as-motion bar confirmed live by the owner. G3 grain PROVEN-UNADOPTED: a working, measured tool with no current application, shelved rather than rejected. G4 spring ADOPTED as the site's arrival and interaction grammar (zeta 0.72, omega-n 9.2, 620ms linear() family, zero JS); framer-motion removed this task and banned as a dependency. THE MINT RESTRAINT LAW: on the noir register mint appears in exactly two places, the active route (braid and map) and the primary CTA, and nowhere else at any opacity or size. N4-A is REVERSED with its receipt - the mobility cards' active state becomes spring physics plus a subtle charcoal elevation rather than neon borders, on the owner's rationale that neon edges on every card turn the page into a laser tag arena: one ring is an instrument, six rings are a game, and the treatment failed on repetition rather than on contrast or craft. The nav's mint underline is retired under the same law; the bar's boundary is carried by glass, structure and the neutral I21 hairline, so I21's mechanism is preserved and only its colour changes. D29's section-5 ring amendment stays on the books but is DORMANT - no sanctioned surface uses a neon ring, it is not repealed, and nothing may cite it as licence today.

decisions.title: The signature, implemented (braid + physics van at route scale)
decisions.summary: WEAVE: the canonical path becomes the serpentine lead of a three-strand weave with companions at phase plus/minus 2pi/3; swing 36px peak-to-peak, wavelength 722px (6 full periods) at 1440 and 1920, polyline sampled at 14px. The swing extends LEFT ONLY and the lead's rightmost x stays exactly gutterX, because the measured room right of the gutter is 30px at every width and the van lane already spends 22 of it. An integer number of periods means the serpentine begins and ends at gutterX, so the terminus cubic is byte-identical to the shipped one. A DEADBAND rather than a clamp: below 12px of room the swing is zero and the route degenerates to exactly the straight line that shipped, because a bare clamp produced a 2 to 7px lateral over a 722px wavelength around VW 1196 to 1220, which reads as a rendering fault rather than a braid. CLEARANCE: pointwise strand-to-text minimum 28.75px at 1024, 1440 and 1920, and not applicable below lg where the route is not rendered - identical to the straight line it replaces, by construction. These numbers are floors. SEAM: hard switch, ruled by arithmetic rather than taste - a blend necessarily paints the ink-register colour onto the paper register for the blend width, and electric mint measures 1.49:1 on paper, so a blend is a contrast violation with a soft edge rather than a stylistic alternative. LIVERY B: the mint outline is CONSTANT and does not switch register, because a 30px object changing colour mid-travel reads as a glitch and the two registers already carry the silhouette differently. PHYSICS: path-time reparameterization, p to s through a precomputed monotone warp, with --route-progress carrying s so the dash, the van and I20 all read one number meaning one thing; dial is lateral cap 0.15 and K 14. The dial is governed by DRIFT rather than ratio, because the van's offset from linear scroll is max deviation times path length and once that approaches a viewport height the van leaves the screen; uncapped the terminus dominates and gives 3.96:1 ratio at 860px of drift, while the cap makes it saturate at the serpentine's level so the alternating fast and slow largely cancel. Shipped and measured: felt ratio 2.12:1, max drift 52px. SCROLL-OBEDIENCE IS LAW: the warp is monotone non-decreasing in scroll and the route never moves on its own; a warp is a reparameterisation, and a route running on its own clock is an animation and a violation. CANONICAL-PATH LAW: exactly one truth, the lead, carrying data-route-canonical with the invariant asserting there is exactly one; companions are decorative siblings never sampled, measured or ridden. FO-1: C4 OBSERVED on the LIVE production site (main @ f0de3c9) on a Lenovo Yoga 7 class Windows machine with basic dedicated graphics - the route line and the livery van sit at visibly different positions at the same scroll, and in one frame the van renders with no line nearby. Owner also reports a bluish panel cast (C3-class, panel-level; a screenshot cannot capture it, so the colour-bench readings on that machine remain the instrument and are pending). MECHANISM NAMED AND SOURCE-VERIFIED in docs/FIELD_OBSERVATIONS.md - git diff f0de3c9..HEAD on RouteOverlay.tsx is EMPTY, so live V1 and current v2 are identical here. One path string serves two renderers in two coordinate systems: the line as SVG path with pathLength=1 inside viewBox 0 0 geo.w geo.h, the van via CSS offset-path in raw pixels. measure() runs on mount and window.resize ONLY (grep-confirmed: no ResizeObserver, no MutationObserver), so docStart/docSpan go stale. THE SOURCE CORRECTED THE CHAT DIAGNOSIS: the SVG carries preserveAspectRatio=none while the host height is FROZEN inline at geo.h and the width is LIVE at w-full, so the axes scale independently - a live-width change (a scrollbar appearing as document height changes) stretches the path NON-UNIFORMLY, which changes arc-length parameterisation, so the line head (dashoffset on the stretched normalised path) and the van (offset-distance on the raw path) are different points, expressing vertically on a long mostly-vertical route. That is the desync. The frozen height is a SEPARATE failure producing the stale band and the van-with-no-line frame. SCHEDULED: W5, with invariant I20 shipping in the same task per D12. NOT ESTABLISHED: which failure dominates on that machine - needs measurement on the machine, not reasoning from source. RESOLVED 2026-08-18 (Task #19). BOTH failure modes were REPRODUCED on the unfixed prod build before anything was changed, deterministically and with no window resize, and re-measured after. Mode 1 (divergence) trigger: change the overlay host's rendered width post-mount, which is what a scrollbar appearing or disappearing does; van-to-drawn-curve distance went 1.52px / 6.08px / 31.67px (at -15 / -60 / -200px) to 0.00px, and the svg CTM went 0.8611 to 1.0000. Mode 2 (stale band) trigger: inject 1500px of document height post-mount; the route's end sat 1536px above the footer seam instead of the intended 36px handoff, and now sits at 36px. ARCHITECTURE: both halves shipped, because the measurements showed the two failures need different medicine. The route svg is now sized in PIXELS (width/height plus inline style equal to geo.w/geo.h, preserveAspectRatio removed, viewBox carrying the same two numbers) so its CTM is forced to identity and the van's raw-pixel offset-path reads the same coordinate system - a stretch is no longer representable. A rAF-debounced ResizeObserver on the document element, the measured region and the host keeps that geometry current on reflows that never resize the window, with an equality guard so an unchanged geometry never re-renders (which also stops the observer feeding itself). The spec's getPointAtLength variant was REJECTED on a perf reading: it would have added a geometry read to every frame to fix the SMALLER of the two failures, while the pixel-sizing route costs nothing per frame and the scroll handler's budget (one rAF, one var write, zero per-frame layout reads) is doctrine. A MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE FO-1 RECORD: the divergence is a PURE HORIZONTAL shear (vertical component stayed within 0.09px in every sample, tracking (1 - ctm.a) * pathX exactly), NOT the arc-length reparameterisation recorded there - the browser parameterises the dash in user space and applies the CTM afterwards. Since this path's x never exceeds ~228, mode 1 is bounded near 32px even for a 200px width error, so mode 2 is the DOMINANT field failure and the only measured mechanism with vertical magnitude.

FO-2: the scrolled-nav bottom edge did not exist on the owner's standard laptop - the OPERATIVE device that set the D23 floors - even though it shipped at --on-ink-border-strong, the owner's own E2-05 floor. Two passes in the same session isolated it: card and grid hairlines EXIST (D23 holds) and the /platform sticky sub-nav rule reads CRISP (no demotion warranted). RESOLVED 2026-08-18 (Task #20). ALL THREE PRIME SUSPECTS WERE ACQUITTED BY MEASUREMENT: the edge was rendered at DSF 1 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 2 on chromium, webkit and firefox and the seam pixel-sampled from the PNG (zero-dep decode via node:zlib), and in all 12 cells the state was ARMED and the painted row matched the token at distance ZERO. Not fractional-DPR erasure, not a failure to arm, not the glass layer swallowing it. THE ACTUAL MECHANISM IS CONTRAST POLARITY: a line is seen when it is a LOCAL EXTREMUM, different from the nearest different value on BOTH sides. Over ink the edge is a local MAX (~4.0) and reads - which is exactly the case the F1 bench fragment tested, since that fragment was titled 'Nav over ink'. Over LIGHT content the same edge sits MONOTONICALLY between a dark bar (L 0.025) and a bright page (L 0.928) at L 0.195, so the eye folds it into the boundary ramp and reads it as antialiasing; measured strength 0.00 at all four DSFs. The owner supplied the control for free: the /platform rule they called CRISP measures as a LOCAL MIN at strength 2.36. THICKENING DOES NOT WORK AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ARGUED: a 2px border scores 0.00 on the light side at all four DSFs, because thickness cannot create an extremum that polarity denies. FIX: a --nav-seam token (rgb(11 21 18 / 0.75)) painted as a hard 0-blur box-shadow hairline below the bar, armed by the same scrolled condition so the page-top no-border design is untouched. Light-side strength 1.92-2.31, comparable to the /platform rule the owner already calls crisp; ink side preserved at 4.27/3.19/2.16/4.26. The border token was NOT changed and the D23 floors were NOT softened.

FO-3: on a Yoga-class laptop the van tracks the straight leg and then IGNORES THE TERMINUS CURVE, continuing straight down while the drawn line turns. Build provenance established by FINGERPRINT rather than by hash: the owner saw the scrolled-nav seam over light content, which does not exist before Task #20, so the build is at or after 9d2e2e3 and FO-1's fixes were PRESENT. HELD, NOT RESOLVED (Task #21). NOT REPRODUCED in any lane: 51 samples across 4 emulation lanes (deviceScaleFactor, Emulation.setPageScaleFactor, Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride, CSS zoom on html) x 3 engines x 3 scroll positions, every one within 1px. THE PRIME SUSPECT WAS NOT CONVICTED AND THE PREDICTION FAILED: the reported signature implies an error proportional to the path x-coordinate, and every sample records dxFromGutter alongside the error - at dxFromGutter 0 and at dxFromGutter 172 the error is the same and it is about zero. offset-path was never rejected; the computed value was read at every sample and was always valid. THE CANDIDATE FIX WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED: offset-path url(#route-path), pointing the van at the rendered path element instead of a copied string, priced well (accepted in all three engines, 0.00px position change on switch, zero per-frame cost against 19us chromium / 44us webkit / 102us firefox for per-frame getPointAtLength) - but it SHIPPED INTO THE CUBE AND I20 FAILED IT. url() has a stale-reference invalidation bug in Chromium and WebKit: when the referenced path element's d changes, the van keeps the OLD geometry, measured at 978px off and PERSISTENT through 1500ms, while firefox invalidates correctly. That is a worse version of the class it was meant to remove, and it is exactly the symptom FO-3 describes. Reverted. The shipped path() assignment is correct BECAUSE it is re-assigned on every geometry change, which forces the invalidation url() skips. NEXT INSTRUMENT: a field console probe (recorded verbatim in docs/FIELD_OBSERVATIONS.md FO-3) to be run on the Yoga at the curve - errorPx is the whole question, and dxFromGutter / errX / errY / ctm / zoom / dpr capture the machine state no emulation lane reproduced. CONVICTED AND FIXED 2026-08-19 (Task #22). The owner ran the console probe on the Yoga at the curve, at browser zoom 100% on Windows 125% scaling (dpr 1.25), build fingerprint preserveAspect=null proving the build was at or after Task #19. It returned progress 0, errX 0.0, errY 2945.6, vvScale 1, svgW 1521px, winW 1536. Read that carefully because it names the mechanism: the shared --route-progress variable read ZERO, the LINE rendered that honestly (undrawn, matching the owner screenshot showing no line), and the VAN, reading the same variable through a different renderer, sat 2945.6px along the route holding a value the variable no longer had. errX 0.0 means the two agree perfectly on the horizontal axis and the entire disagreement is distance ALONG the route. Not paint, not geometry - STATE: one variable, two renderers, one of them no longer listening. The owner zoom ladder correlates exactly with the EFFECTIVE fractional scale: 100 percent x 1.25 = 1.25 large gap, 90 x 1.25 = 1.125 small gap, 80 x 1.25 = 1.00 perfect - a rasterisation-boundary signature. THE CHROMIUM-INTERNAL INVALIDATION PATH REMAINS DELIBERATELY UNPROVEN: it was never reproducible in lab (Task #21, 51 samples, 4 emulation lanes, 3 engines, all within 1px), so it could not be instrumented, so claiming to have diagnosed it would be worse than saying so. THE FIX IS ARCHITECTURAL - the class was removed instead. The van is now a <g> INSIDE the route svg, in the same user space, positioned per frame by an SVG transform written from the same number in the same frame as the line's dash. offset-path, offset-distance, offset-rotate, offset-anchor, the imperative offsetPath assignment and the @supports display gate are all gone. There is no second renderer left to desync. ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-20 (Task #25), and it was neither zoom nor dpr. The shipped rule was stroke-dasharray 1 with stroke-dashoffset calc(1 - var(--route-progress, 1)). As a CSS PROPERTY, stroke-dashoffset takes a length-percentage and a bare number is NOT a length; stroke-dasharray is the lenient one because it genuinely accepts a number, which is why only the offset broke. Blink and WebKit coerce the number and hide it, serialising calc(0.729646px) and 0.72968px. GECKO IS STRICT AND CORRECT: it drops the declaration, the offset falls back to its initial value 0, and with dasharray 1 that paints the ENTIRE path. So Gecko rendered a fully drawn line beside a correctly placed van, which is exactly the reported LINE-FULL vs VAN-MID signature. Measured at dpr 1, 1.5 and 2 in Gecko with identical results, so device pixel ratio was a red herring and engine strictness was the variable. FIX: multiply by a unit so the value is a real length. Verified in all three engines at dpr 2 and w1542: dashoffset now serialises 0.618027px, 0.618117px and 0.619808px, lineP equals the variable, head Y equals van Y, gap 0. I20 now parses the computed dashoffset, stripping calc first, and fails if the line disagrees with the variable by more than 0.02; since Firefox is already a cube engine, that assertion would have caught this on the day it shipped.
